research_mode: official Home Office, ONS and GOV.UK primary methodology only; each claim has a fail-closed limitation; no parcel result, exact incident location, local risk score, candidate value or business result claimed

sources.name: Two principal crime sources
verified_claims: ONS crime statistics combine the Crime Survey for England and Wales with police recorded crime.
limitations: The two sources measure different populations and processes and should not be treated as interchangeable.

sources.name: CSEW reference period
verified_claims: The CSEW asks household residents about crimes experienced during the 12 months before interview.
limitations: The survey reference window does not identify a single calendar month for each incident.

sources.name: CSEW population and offence exclusions
verified_claims: The main CSEW excludes crimes against businesses, people outside households, homicide and offences often described as victimless such as drug possession.
limitations: The absence of an estimate does not imply that excluded crimes or populations experienced no crime.

sources.name: CSEW response-rate context
verified_claims: The provisional CSEW response rate for year ending March 2026 was 48%, and ONS reported that its quality review found little impact on estimate reliability.
limitations: The lower response rate remains a quality consideration and does not eliminate sampling or non-response uncertainty.

sources.name: CSEW long-term series
verified_claims: CSEW estimates support analysis of long-term crime trends from year ending December 1981 to year ending March 2026.
limitations: The long series does not make every offence definition or module directly comparable across all years.

sources.name: Police recorded crime force coverage
verified_claims: Police recorded crime supplied to ONS covers 43 territorial forces in England and Wales plus British Transport Police.
limitations: Force coverage does not include offences never reported to or recorded by police.

sources.name: Notifiable-offence scope
verified_claims: Police recorded crime coverage is defined by the Notifiable Offence List and excludes non-notifiable matters such as parking offences and anti-social behaviour.
limitations: Police recorded crime totals are not a complete count of every incident handled by public authorities.

sources.name: CSEW accredited status
verified_claims: CSEW estimates are accredited official statistics and were independently reviewed by the Office for Statistics Regulation in October 2024.
limitations: Accreditation does not remove survey sampling, recall or coverage limitations.

sources.name: CSEW long-term trend strength
verified_claims: ONS describes the CSEW as its most reliable indicator for long-term trends in common crimes experienced by the general household population.
limitations: The strength applies to crimes and populations covered by the survey, not every crime type or local area.

sources.name: CSEW sampling and recall error
verified_claims: CSEW estimates are subject to sampling error and non-sampling error, including respondents' recall of past events.
limitations: Point estimates must not be represented as exact counts without uncertainty.

sources.name: Low-volume CSEW variability
verified_claims: The CSEW sample produces substantial variability for infrequent crime types, making short-term trends difficult to detect.
limitations: Small apparent movements in rare crimes may be statistical noise rather than real change.

sources.name: Police data strength for well-recorded crime
verified_claims: For offences that are well reported and accurately recorded, police recorded crime can provide a good picture of volume.
limitations: This strength cannot be assumed for offences with low reporting or inconsistent recording.

sources.name: Police-demand insight
verified_claims: Police recorded crime provides information about demands placed on police and where policing effort is spent.
limitations: Police demand is not equivalent to underlying victimisation or parcel-level risk.

sources.name: Police recorded crime trend limitation
verified_claims: For many crime types, police recorded crime is not a reliable measure of levels or trends because it depends on reporting, police activity and recording practice.
limitations: A recorded increase cannot be attributed solely to increased offending.

sources.name: Police recorded crime designation
verified_claims: Police recorded crime does not currently meet the required standard for designation as accredited official statistics because of quality and consistency concerns.
limitations: Official-statistics publication does not justify treating every force and year as equally comparable.

sources.name: Combined-source coverage
verified_claims: Using CSEW and police recorded crime together generally improves coverage of crime against the public, especially physical harm, loss and property damage.
limitations: Combining sources requires preserving their separate definitions, populations and uncertainties.

sources.name: CSEW inclusion of unreported crime
verified_claims: For its covered population and offences, the CSEW includes crimes not reported to or recorded by police.
limitations: Survey inclusion of unreported crime does not produce exact local incident locations.

sources.name: Independent-check role
verified_claims: ONS describes the CSEW as an independent check on police recorded crime figures.
limitations: A discrepancy between sources requires methodological analysis rather than choosing whichever value is larger.

sources.name: Sensitive self-completion modules
verified_claims: Domestic and sexual violence are collected through separate self-completion questions, and age coverage of these modules expanded over time.
limitations: Results from changing module coverage should not be compared without accounting for questionnaire and eligibility changes.

sources.name: Fraud and computer-misuse module history
verified_claims: Fraud and computer-misuse questions were added to the CSEW in October 2015 and later incorporated into headline estimates after a full year of data.
limitations: Headline crime before and after inclusion of these offences is not directly like-for-like without adjustment.
